THE RIVER BRIDE PART 2 - THE LAST NIGHT.t: THE RIVER BRIDE PART 2 - THE LAST NIGHT
THE RIVER BRIDE PART 2 - THE LAST NIGHT.short: One year later, Adaeze risks everything to be human wife for one night. But Mamala wants to kill her, Amara wants to steal Emeka, and little Zara is dying.
THE RIVER BRIDE PART 2 - THE LAST NIGHT.long: Anniversary night Adaeze became River Bride. River God allows one night on land but warns she will die as human. Inside river, jealous first wife MAMALA plots to drown her boyfriend and kill her. In Umunzu village, Emeka waits 2 years, Okonkwo advises to forget, Amara secretly loves Emeka. Midnight Adaeze appears shining, but little Zara 7 years burning with fever. Adaeze heals her breaking river law. Mamala attacks with snakes in hair, mother spirit NGOZI appears. River God forgives and gives one beautiful night as husband and wife.
THE RIVER BRIDE PART 2 - THE LAST NIGHT.full:
*SYNOPSIS:* One year later, Adaeze wants to risk everything to be a human wife for one night. But the River God's first wife, Mamala, wants to kill her, Amara wants to steal Emeka, and little Zara is dying.

*FULL STORY:*

*NARRATOR:* It was the anniversary night. The night Adaeze became the River Bride. Inside the river palace, Adaeze sat on her throne, crying. Her crown was heavy.

*RIVER GOD:* Adaeze, you are crying again. Tonight you can go to land. But I warned you. If you go to see that boy, I will not allow you to come back. You will die as a human.

*ADAEZE:* Then let me die. I don't want to be a goddess forever. I want to be a wife for one night.

*NARRATOR:* Inside the deeper part of the river, someone was listening. It was MAMALA, the first wife of the River God. She was very beautiful, but her heart was full of jealousy.

*MAMALA:* (Angry) So this small human girl wants to leave our world? Good. Tonight, I will make sure she never returns. I will drown her boyfriend and kill her.

*NARRATOR:* On land, in Umunzu village, Emeka was waiting by the river. He had not married for two years. His best friend, OKONKWO, came to meet him.

*OKONKWO:* Emeka, my brother, you are here again? It is midnight. This girl is now a goddess. Forget her.

*EMEKA:* I can never forget her, Okonkwo. She said she would come every year. I will wait.

*OKONKWO:* And what about AMARA? That girl loves you. She brings you food every day. She is a good girl.

*EMEKA:* My heart belongs to Adaeze only.

*NARRATOR:* In another part of the village, AMARA was watching them from behind a tree. She was crying.

*AMARA:* Emeka, I have loved you for three years. Why can't you see me? Tonight, I will follow you to the river. I will make sure Adaeze leaves you alone.

*NARRATOR:* At midnight, the water began to spin. Adaeze came out, wearing her white wrapper, shining like moonlight. She was still 19.

*EMEKA:* Adaeze! You came!

*ADAEZE:* Emeka!

*NARRATOR:* They hugged. But before they could talk, they heard a small voice crying. It was LITTLE ZARA, the 7-year-old girl, coughing near the river bank.

*ADAEZE:* Zara? What are you doing here at night? You are burning with fever!

*LITTLE ZARA:* Mama Adaeze, I am sick. My mother said only the river goddess can save me. Please help me.

*ADAEZE:* Oh no. River God said if I touch any human tonight, I will lose my powers.

*EMEKA:* We must save her, Adaeze.

*ADAEZE:* (Touches Zara's head and prays) River, please heal this child.

*NARRATOR:* Immediately, Zara's fever disappeared. But inside the river, MAMALA felt it.

*MAMALA:* She used her power on land! Now she is weak! This is my chance.

*NARRATOR:* Suddenly, the river became rough. A big wave came out. MAMALA appeared, with snakes in her hair.

*MAMALA:* Adaeze! You are a selfish bride! You healed a human child without permission! You have broken the river law! Now you must die!

*ADAEZE:* Who are you?

*MAMALA:* I am Mamala! The first wife! The queen before you came! Tonight, I will take your life and take your boyfriend!

*EMEKA:* Leave her alone!

*OKONKWO:* (Running with his cutlass) Emeka! What is happening?

*NARRATOR:* Mamala raised her hand and the water held Emeka and Okonkwo, so they could not move.

*MAMALA:* You cannot fight me, humans!

*NARRATOR:* Adaeze was afraid and weak. She was about to give up. Then, a soft light appeared on the water. It was a woman in white. It was NGOZI, Adaeze's mother who died many years ago.

*NGOZI:* Adaeze, my daughter.

*ADAEZE:* Mama? Mama! Is that you?

*NGOZI:* Yes, my child. I have been watching you from the world of spirits. You have a pure heart. You saved Zara. That is true love, not selfish love. The river loves a pure heart.

*MAMALA:* Ngozi! You cannot save her! She broke the law!

*NGOZI:* No, Mamala. She followed the highest law — love. River God! Come and see what your bride did!

*NARRATOR:* The RIVER GOD appeared, tall and shining. He saw Zara, now healed and smiling. He saw Emeka who still waited after two years. He saw Adaeze who risked her throne to save a child.

*RIVER GOD:* Mamala, leave them. Adaeze has shown me what human love means. It is not selfish. It gives.

*MAMALA:* But you promised me she would die if she went to land!

*RIVER GOD:* I was jealous. I was wrong. Adaeze, you saved a child. You did not use your night for yourself. For that, I will forgive you.

*ADAEZE:* Thank you, my lord.

*RIVER GOD:* Tonight, I give you a new gift. You can be human for one full night. No curse. You and Emeka can be husband and wife till morning. And little Zara will never be sick again.

*LITTLE ZARA:* Thank you, Mama Adaeze!

*NARRATOR:* Mamala was angry and disappeared into the deep water forever.

*NGOZI:* My daughter, I am proud of you. Be happy tonight. (Her spirit disappears)

*NARRATOR:* Amara, who was watching from the bush, saw everything. She started crying and left quietly. She understood that Emeka and Adaeze's love was true.

*AMARA:* I will find my own love. Let them be happy.

*NARRATOR:* That night, Adaeze and Emeka finally became husband and wife by the river side, under the moon. Okonkwo played music and Zara danced.

It was their last night as humans, but it was the most beautiful night in Umunzu.

But in the morning, Adaeze had to return to the river...

*TO BE CONTINUED IN RIVER BRIDE PART 3...*

THE RIVER BRIDE PART 3 - THE FINAL END.t: THE RIVER BRIDE PART 3 - THE FINAL END
THE RIVER BRIDE PART 3 - THE FINAL END.short: Morning has come. Adaeze must return to river forever after one night as Emeka's wife. But Mamala returns from deep water to flood Umunzu and kill Zara. Will River God finally free Adaeze?
THE RIVER BRIDE PART 3 - THE FINAL END.long: Morning after one night as husband and wife. Adaeze must return to river forever. Mamala did not disappear in Part 2 - hid in deep water for revenge and floods Umunzu. Zara trapped on rock, Obinna house flooding, Igwe Okoro shouting. Adaeze powerless as human. Priestess Nneka tries to stop Mamala, mother ghost NGOZI returns stronger. River God appears angry, turns Mamala to stone forever at river bottom. Frees Adaeze to be human forever, gives double wedding Adaeze/Emeka and Amara/Okonkwo. Mamala stone gives healing power.
THE RIVER BRIDE PART 3 - THE FINAL END.full:
*SYNOPSIS:*
The morning has come. Adaeze must return to the river forever after her one night as Emeka's wife. But Mamala returns from deep water to flood Umunzu and kill Zara. Will River God finally free Adaeze?

*FULL STORY PART 3 - FINAL:*

NARRATOR: Morning was coming in Umunzu. Sun was rising over the river. Birds were singing. Adaeze and Emeka were still by the riverbank, holding each other. Their one night as husband and wife was finished.

ADAEZE: Emeka, sun is coming. I must return. River God said I have till morning. Morning has come.

EMEKA: No! I will not let you go! Last night you were my wife! You slept in my arms! Now you want to leave me again to be queen of water?

ADAEZE: If I don't go, he will be angry. He will punish the village.

EMEKA: Then let him punish me! I will enter river with you! If you go, I go! Even if I drown!

NARRATOR: Inside the river, someone heard that. It was MAMALA. She did not disappear forever in Part 2. She hid in deep water, waiting for revenge.

MAMALA: (From deep water, angry) So she enjoyed one night? Good! Now I will destroy everything she loves! I will flood Umunzu!

NARRATOR: Suddenly, river started shaking. Water rose very fast. It was flooding.

OKONKWO: (Running) Emeka! Flood! Water is entering village!

IGWE OKORO: (Shouting from village square) Everyone run! River is angry again! Take your children!

OBINNA: (Adaeze's mother, crying) Adaeze! Where are you! Water is taking my house!

LITTLE ZARA: (Screaming, trapped on small rock in river) Mama Adaeze! Help! Water is carrying me!

ADAEZE: Zara! Mama Obinna!

EMEKA: We must save them! But I cannot swim fast!

NARRATOR: Adaeze tried to use her power, but she was now weak. She was almost human. She could not stop flood.

ADAEZE: I have no power! I am human now!

MAMALA: (Appearing from flood with snakes in hair, laughing) Yes! You are human now! Weak! Watch me drown your Zara! Watch me kill your village! This is what happens when you steal my husband's love!

NARRATOR: At that moment, PRIESTESS NNEKA came running from shrine with her white chalk and palm leaves.

PRIESTESS NNEKA: Mamala! Stop! The river has taken enough! I am Priestess of this land! I command you by the old gods! Stop!

MAMALA: You? Small priestess? You have no power over me!

NARRATOR: Then, bright white light appeared over the flooded river. It was NGOZI, Adaeze's mother ghost, shining stronger than ever before.

NGOZI: Mamala! Leave my daughter and my people!

MAMALA: Ngozi! You again! You are dead!

NGOZI: I am dead, but mother love never dies. River God! Come and see what your first wife is doing to innocent children!

NARRATOR: RIVER GOD appeared from water, very tall, his golden crown shining, his eyes red with anger. Water stopped shaking when he came.

RIVER GOD: Mamala! What are you doing?! In Part 2, I forgave Adaeze because she showed true love! I gave them one night! Why are you flooding humans again?!

MAMALA: Because you love her more than me! For 100 years I was queen! You never gave me one night on land!

RIVER GOD: I gave you palace! I gave you power! But you never learned to give, only to take! You want to kill a child Zara? For that, you will no longer be queen! You will become stone at bottom of river! Forever! People will see you as warning!

MAMALA: No! My lord! Please! Noooo!

NARRATOR: River God raised his hand. Thunder shouted. Mamala screamed as her blue body turned to stone. Snakes turned to rocks. She sank to bottom of river and became rock forever, with eyes open, lying under water. Flood stopped immediately. Water went back to normal. Zara was safe.

LITTLE ZARA: (Coughing but alive) Mama Adaeze! Water left!

ADAEZE: (Hugging Zara) Zara! You are alive!

OBINNA: My daughter! (Runs and hugs Adaeze)

IGWE OKORO: The flood has stopped! The river is calm! Priestess Nneka, thank the gods!

PRIESTESS NNEKA: It is not me, Igwe. It is true love that calmed river.

NARRATOR: River God looked at Adaeze and Emeka holding each other, wet from flood. He looked at Ngozi spirit, Obinna mother, and little Zara.

RIVER GOD: Adaeze... In Part 1, I took you because I was lonely. In Part 2, you risked everything to save a child Zara, not yourself. You showed me what human love means. It gives. It does not take.

ADAEZE: My lord...

RIVER GOD: Today, I free you. You are no longer River Bride. You are human forever. You will marry your Emeka. You will have children. You will grow old and die as human. And my river will never take a bride again. Rain will come every year in Umunzu because you taught me love.

EMEKA: (Kneeling, crying) Thank you! Thank you, River God!

RIVER GOD: And for Mamala's evil, I will make her stone give healing power. Any sick child who touches river where she lies will be healed.

NGOZI: (Smiling and fading slowly) My daughter, I am proud. My work is done. I can rest now in peace. Be happy, Adaeze. Tell Obinna I love her.

OBINNA: Ngozi? My sister? I hear you!

NGOZI: (Disappears forever, with light)

RIVER GOD: (To Emeka) Take care of her, hunter. (Slowly turns to water and disappears)

NARRATOR: That evening, Igwe Okoro made the biggest feast in Umunzu history. Drums were beating. Women were dancing. Adaeze wore her mother's white wrapper. Emeka wore his hunter best cloth with leopard skin.

IGWE OKORO: Today, we have two weddings! Adaeze and Emeka! And my daughter Amara and Okonkwo!

AMARA: (Shy, holding Okonkwo hand) I finally found love that loves me back.

OKONKWO: And I will love you forever, Amara.

NARRATOR: Priestess Nneka blessed both couples. Little Zara danced in middle.

ADAEZE: (Looking at river) Emeka, I was River Bride for two years, but I will be your wife for life.

EMEKA: And I waited for you at river for two years, and I will wait for you forever.

NARRATOR: And so, story of River Bride ended. Not with death, but with love winning. Every year, Adaeze and Emeka go to river and drop white flowers where River God disappeared. And deep at bottom, Mamala stone still lies, watching, but can never hurt anyone again.

THE END.

*A GHANAIAN FOLKLORE - 2026*

THE STOLEN BABY.short: After 4 years of childlessness in Bantama, Kumasi, Zara finally gives birth at Komfo Anokye - but her baby wrapped in YELLOW KENTE CLOTH is stolen at 3:15 AM by her own mother-in-law and sold to a rich barren CEO in Accra. One year later, a gossip in the hospital corridor reveals the truth. Will a mother's love find her stolen baby?
THE STOLEN BABY.long:
THE STOLEN BABY is a powerful Ghanaian folktale by ZeenatFlix about motherhood, betrayal, and the yellow kente cloth that connects two mothers.

Zara (24) and Ethan Boakye (28) were KNUST's best couple from Bantama, Kumasi. After 3 years of mockery for childlessness, Zara finally gets pregnant. Her mother sews a special YELLOW KENTE CLOTH with 'Abena' stitched inside for the baby.

On labour night at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, Zara delivers a healthy boy, Baby Jaden. Ethan takes a photo and goes to buy koko. At 3:15 AM, Mama Celestine Boakye (Ethan's mother), who visited a mallam in Tafo, bribes Dr. Nadia GH₵30,000 and Nurse Serwaa GH₵10,000 to steal the baby in the yellow kente inside a basket. They tell Zara it was a phantom pregnancy.

The baby is sold for GH₵80,000 to Mrs. Arabella Sedinam Laryea (42), CEO of Laryea Cosmetics, barren for 15 years in Airport Residential, Accra, and her billionaire husband Mr. Frederick Laryea. They name him Jayden Laryea and keep the yellow kente.

One year later, Zara working as a cleaner in the hospital overhears Dr. Nadia and Nurse Serwaa gossiping - your poster moment. She travels to Accra, finds the proof inside the yellow kente cloth with 'Abena' stitched, DNA 99.9% match, and a deathbed confession video.

Will the judge return the baby to its blood mother? Will Arabella who loved Jayden for a year let go? This emotional Ghana folktale based in Kumasi and Accra shows that a mother's love never forgets. 15,000 babies are stolen every year in Africa.
THE STOLEN BABY.full:
NARRATOR: Bantama, Kumasi. Ethan Boakye and Zara were the best couple in Bantama. Everyone knew them.

ZARA: Ethan, we met in KNUST level 200, 2 years dating, everyone admires us.

ETHAN BOAKYE: Zara, I will marry you. You are my queen.

NARRATOR: SCENE 1 - BEST COUPLE IN BANTAMA - THE WEDDING. Beautiful wedding at Bantama Church.

PASTOR: At Bantama Church, do you Ethan Boakye take Zara to be your wife?

ETHAN BOAKYE: Yes, I do!

PASTOR: Do you Zara take Ethan to be your husband?

ZARA: Yes, I do! I am so happy!

NARRATOR: Everyone claps. Big wedding reception in Bantama. Family dancing. Mama Celestine Boakye pretends to be happy.

MAMA CELESTINE BOAKYE: My son has married, I am happy. (Fake smile)

ZARA: Mama, thank you for coming.

NARRATOR: After wedding, they try for baby.

ZARA: Ethan, 1 year no baby, what is wrong?

ETHAN BOAKYE: Let's go to hospital for test.

ZARA: 2 years, no baby, family mocks me.

MAMA CELESTINE BOAKYE: Barren woman! Two years no child in my son's house!

ETHAN BOAKYE: Mama stop insulting my wife!

ZARA: (cries every night) Ethan, maybe I am barren.

ETHAN BOAKYE: (holds her every night) No my love, God will give us baby.

ZARA: 3 years now, mockery, insults, hospital tests, no baby. I am tired.

NARRATOR: SCENE 2 - AFTER 4 YEARS - PRAYER ANSWERED. Morning in Bantama, house of Zara and Ethan.

ZARA: (vomits) Ugh, ugh, I am vomiting morning morning.

ETHAN BOAKYE: My wife sick? Let me rush you to Komfo Anokye Hospital now!

DR. NADIA: (checking test) Madam Zara, you are finally pregnant after 4 years! Congratulations!

ZARA: What! Doctor! Are you sure! After 4 years!

ETHAN BOAKYE: (screaming, dancing in Komfo Anokye corridor) My wife is pregnant! After 4 years of mockery! God has answered!

ZARA: (dancing with Ethan) We are finally pregnant!

NARRATOR: Ethan organizes big baby shower in Bantama. Everyone comes, food, drinks, jollof, music.

ETHAN BOAKYE: Everyone in Bantama, my wife is pregnant! Come to baby shower!

ZARA'S MOTHER: (sewing yellow kente cloth) My daughter, I sewed special YELLOW KENTE CLOTH with name Abena stitched inside for my grandson.

ZARA: Thank you Mama, it is beautiful.

NARRATOR: Mama Celestine Boakye smiles outside at shower, but later that night she visits a mallam in Tafo.

MAMA CELESTINE BOAKYE: Mallam, tell me about this baby my daughter-in-law is carrying.

MALLAM: This child will take your son away from you and bring shame to your family. This child must not stay alive in this family.

MAMA CELESTINE BOAKYE: Then baby must disappear. I will make it disappear at hospital.

NARRATOR: SCENE 3 - LABOUR NIGHT. 2 AM, Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, labour ward, maternity ward sign.

ZARA: (in pain, sweating) Ah! Ethan! The pain is too much!

ETHAN BOAKYE: (praying outside labour ward) God, save my wife and child! Please!

DR. NADIA: Madam push! Push! I can see head!

NURSE SERWAA: Push Zara!

ZARA: (screams, baby cries loud) Waaa! Waaa!

DR. NADIA: It is healthy baby boy! Beautiful boy! After 4 years!

ZARA: My baby! Give me my baby!

DR. NADIA: (wraps baby in special YELLOW KENTE CLOTH) We wrap him in special yellow kente your mother sewed with Abena stitched inside.

ZARA: My son, my yellow cloth, thank you.

ETHAN BOAKYE: (enters, taking photo with phone) My son! Baby Jaden! I will name him Jaden! Let me take photo for family! I go buy koko and bread for you Zara, wait small!

NARRATOR: Ethan goes to buy koko and bread at 2 AM. Zara given injection to sleep.

ZARA: I am feeling sleepy...

DR. NADIA: Sleep small, you need rest after labour.

NARRATOR: SCENE 4 - THE STEALING - 3:15 AM. Zara sleeps deeply.

MAMA CELESTINE BOAKYE: (enters quietly with traditional basket) Doctor, ready? GH₵30,000 for you, GH₵10,000 for Nurse Serwaa as we agreed.

DR. NADIA: Yes Mama Celestine, bring basket. I turned off CCTV. No evidence.

NURSE SERWAA: Give me baby, I will carry him still wrapped in YELLOW KENTE inside basket.

MAMA CELESTINE BOAKYE: Good. My grandson sleeping in yellow cloth. We walk through back corridor now, quick quick.

NARRATOR: Poster moment - old woman with basket, baby in yellow cloth sleeping, walking through dark hospital corridor at 3:15 AM, CCTV off.

NARRATOR: SCENE 5 - THE LIE. Zara wakes up, hands reaching out like poster.

ZARA: (waking, hands reaching) My baby? Where is my baby? Where is my yellow cloth? Nurse! Where is my baby in yellow kente!

DR. NADIA: (with straight face) Madam Zara, you never gave birth. It was phantom pregnancy from drugs we gave you. You were dreaming because you wanted baby for 4 years.

ZARA: No! You are lying! There is blood on bed! I gave birth! I held my baby! Where is my yellow kente! My mother sewed Abena inside!

DR. NADIA: Madam, stop shouting, there was no baby, no yellow cloth.

NARRATOR: Ethan returns, koko in hand, phone gone.

ETHAN BOAKYE: Zara where is my phone? I left it here to take baby photo! Where is photo of my son?

MAMA CELESTINE BOAKYE: (who stole phone to delete baby photo) My son, there was no baby, Zara is hallucinating, she is mad. Doctor said phantom pregnancy.

ZARA: Ethan believe me! I gave birth! They stole our baby in yellow kente!

ETHAN BOAKYE: Zara? Mama says no baby?

NARRATOR: SCENE 6 - INTRODUCING THE RICHEST COUPLE. Airport Residential, Accra. Big mansion, Laryea Mansion.

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: (42, CEO of Laryea Cosmetics, barren 15 years, crying in luxury bedroom) Frederick, 15 years barren, 3 failed IVFs, everyone calls me barren CEO, I am tired.

MR. FREDERICK LARYEA: (48, kind billionaire, owns Laryea Estates) My love Arabella, don't cry. Let's adopt legally. God will give us child.

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: I just want to be a mother, Frederick, just one baby.

NARRATOR: SCENE 7 - THE ILLEGAL DEAL.

DR. NADIA: (calling at night) Hello Mr. Frederick Laryea? I am Dr. Nadia from Komfo Anokye. I have newborn baby boy, mother died after birth, legal adoption available but pay GH₵80,000 for fast papers tonight.

MR. FREDERICK LARYEA: Arabella! Baby boy! Mother died! Legal adoption! GH₵80,000 for fast papers! Should we?

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: Yes! Pay! Pay! I want baby!

NARRATOR: That same night, Baby Jaden arrives in Accra inside basket wrapped in same YELLOW KENTE CLOTH.

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: (carrying baby) Oh my baby! Finally! But why yellow kente cloth?

DR. NADIA: Mother was Ashanti woman from Kumasi, she left this yellow kente before dying. Keep it as memory of her.

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: It is beautiful yellow kente, I will keep it safe.

NARRATOR: SCENE 8 - JAYDEN LARYEA. One month later, big naming ceremony in Accra, Airport Residential.

MR. FREDERICK LARYEA: Today we name our son Jayden Laryea! Big party!

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: My son Jayden, I love you like my own blood, I will never leave you.

NARRATOR: Frederick builds nursery worth GH₵100,000 cedis, toys, clothes, golden cot. Arabella loves him like own blood.

NARRATOR: SCENE 9 - ONE YEAR OF MADNESS. Kumasi, Bantama.

ETHAN BOAKYE: Zara, my mother said you never gave birth, you are mad woman, I believe my mother, I am leaving you, divorcing you.

ZARA: Ethan no! I gave birth at Komfo Anokye! Our baby was wrapped in yellow kente with Abena stitched!

MAMA CELESTINE BOAKYE: She is mad, my son, leave this mad woman.

NARRATOR: Family calls Zara mad woman. Zara loses husband, house, everything. She takes job as cleaner at Komfo Anokye to find truth.

ZARA: I will work as cleaner, I will clean every night, searching records, searching for my yellow kente baby.

NARRATOR: SCENE 10 - THE GOSSIP.

ZARA: (mopping corridor night shift) I must mop this maternity corridor.

DR. NADIA: (in blue uniform gossiping with Nurse Serwaa, whispering exactly like the poster right side) That Laryea baby in Accra, that yellow kente baby we sold, Madam Arabella doesn't know it's stolen from Bantama woman.

NURSE SERWAA: Shh! Keep voice down! That baby we sold for GH₵80,000, remember? The Bantama woman's baby with yellow kente, that baby is now Jayden Laryea in Accra.

ZARA: (drops mop loudly, metal sound) What! Yellow kente baby! Laryea baby in Accra! My baby!

DR. NADIA: Who is there! Who heard us!

ZARA: (runs away crying) I must go to Accra! My baby is in Accra!

NARRATOR: SCENE 11 - JOURNEY TO ACCRA.

ZARA: (at Kejetia market selling her only kente) I sell my only kente to buy VIP bus ticket to Accra, I have only baby's sock as proof.

BUS DRIVER: VIP bus Kumasi to Accra! One seat!

NARRATOR: 6 hours journey. Zara stands outside Laryea mansion gate, Airport Residential, big gate, security.

ZARA: (looking through gate) That is... that is my baby! Jaden!

NARRATOR: Through gate, she sees 1-year-old Jaden in garden calling Arabella Mama.

BABY JADEN: Mama! Mama!

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: Yes my Jayden! My son!

ZARA: (faints at gate) That's my son! My yellow kente baby! (Faints)

SECURITY: Madam! Madam! Are you okay? Wake up!

NARRATOR: SCENE 12 - TWO MOTHERS, ONE BABY.

ZARA: (enters mansion begging, kneeling) Please! That's my baby! That's my yellow kente! His name is Jaden! I gave birth at Komfo Anokye! I am Zara from Bantama!

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: (slaps her hard) How dare you call my son stolen! This is my legally adopted son Jayden Laryea! I have court adoption papers! Security! Throw this mad woman out!

SECURITY: Madam leave!

MR. FREDERICK LARYEA: (comes out from mansion, sees Zara's face, sees Jaden's face - exact copy, same nose) Wait! Wait! Security stop! Stop! Let her speak! Madam, how do you prove? We have legal papers from court.

ZARA: (crying) Sir please, check the yellow kente cloth! My mother stitched Abena inside it! Abena is my mother's name! Check inside the cloth!

NARRATOR: SCENE 13 - THE YELLOW CLOTH PROOF.

MR. FREDERICK LARYEA: (runs inside to wardrobe, brings out same YELLOW KENTE CLOTH) Let me check this cloth.

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: Frederick what are you doing? That is my son's cloth!

MR. FREDERICK LARYEA: (turning yellow kente inside, searching, finds small stitching) It says... Abena... small stitching... Abena stitched inside... (Silence in whole mansion, birds stop)

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: (collapses on floor crying loudly) No! No! No! My son! My Jayden!

ZARA: (crying) That is my mother's stitching! That is my yellow kente! That is my baby! That proves he is my son!

NARRATOR: SCENE 14 - DNA.

MR. FREDERICK LARYEA: I will do secret DNA test to be sure. Give me your hair, Zara.

ZARA: Take my hair! Take everything! He is my son!

MR. FREDERICK LARYEA: (at private lab in Accra) Doctor, test this woman's hair vs my son Jayden's saliva.

DOCTOR: Result: 99.9% match. She is biological mother. This boy is her son.

MR. FREDERICK LARYEA: (confronts Dr. Nadia at hospital with voice recorder hidden) Dr. Nadia, tell me truth about yellow kente baby or I call police and you go to jail 20 years!

DR. NADIA: (scared, confessing on recording) Okay okay! I confess! Mama Celestine Boakye bribed me GH₵30,000 and Nurse Serwaa GH₵10,000 to steal baby at 3:15 AM from Zara! We turned off CCTV! We carried baby in basket with yellow kente! We sold to you for GH₵80,000!

MR. FREDERICK LARYEA: (plays recording to Arabella at home) Arabella, listen to this recording. Baby is stolen. We paid 80,000 thinking legal, but it was stolen from Bantama.

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: (cries 3 hours holding Jaden tight, not letting go) I paid 80,000, I thought it was legal adoption! I just wanted to be a mother! I have loved him for one year like my own blood! I changed his diapers! I fed him!

NARRATOR: SCENE 15 - DEATHBED CONFESSION. Kumasi.

MAMA CELESTINE BOAKYE: (gets stroke, on deathbed at home, calls Ethan and whole family, breathing hard) Ethan... everyone come... I must confess before I die.

ETHAN BOAKYE: Mother what is it?

MAMA CELESTINE BOAKYE: I... I stole Zara's baby... I bribed doctor... I recorded video that night as insurance against Dr. Nadia if she betrays me... Watch...

NARRATOR: She shows video on old phone - video shows her at 3:15 AM carrying basket with yellow cloth out of Komfo Anokye back corridor, baby crying inside yellow kente.

ETHAN BOAKYE: (crying, falls on knees) Mother how could you! You destroyed my family! You made me leave my wife! I must call Zara in Accra now!

NARRATOR: SCENE 16 - ARREST.

POLICE: (at Komfo Anokye) Dr. Nadia and Nurse Serwaa, you are under arrest for child trafficking, baby theft, corruption.

DR. NADIA: We confess! Mama Celestine paid us GH₵30,000 and GH₵10,000!

NURSE SERWAA: We confess! We sold baby for GH₵80,000 to Laryeas!

POLICE: You will go to jail 15 years.

NARRATOR: SCENE 17 - FINAL JUDGMENT. Court in Accra, High Court.

JUDGE: Two mothers crying in court, both holding one hand of Jaden wrapped in same YELLOW KENTE CLOTH. Court has seen DNA 99.9% match, video of stealing at 3:15 AM, confession recording. Blood is blood. Baby returns to biological mother Zara Amoah from Bantama. Dr. Nadia and Nurse Serwaa 15 years prison. Mama Celestine already dead.

ZARA: (crying holding baby) Thank you judge! My baby! My yellow kente baby is back!

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: (crying) No! My Jayden! My son for one year!

NARRATOR: SCENE 18 - GOODBYE. Outside court, Airport Residential mansion.

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: (kisses Jaden last time on forehead, returns yellow kente cloth to Zara with tears) I kept it safe for one year, I washed it every week, I loved him, here take your yellow kente, take your son.

ZARA: Thank you for loving my son when I was not there.

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: I am sorry, I did not know he was stolen, I thought legal. Take GH₵50,000 as apology for pain I caused.

MR. FREDERICK LARYEA: Zara, Ethan, I offer Ethan job as Project Manager in Laryea Estates, GH₵10,000 salary, and I promise to be Jaden's Godfather forever. Let us stay family, not enemies.

ETHAN BOAKYE: Thank you sir, thank you for taking care of my son.

NARRATOR: SCENE 19 - REUNION HAPPY ENDING. Last scene like your poster but happy.

ZARA: (on hospital bed at Komfo Anokye but now smiling, holding Jaden wrapped in yellow kente, Ethan hugging them both) My baby, my yellow kente, you are home! After one year!

ETHAN BOAKYE: My wife, my son, forgive me for not believing you, for leaving you.

BABY JADEN: (laughing) Mama! Dada!

MR. FREDERICK LARYEA: (watching from car outside with Arabella, crying but happy baby found real mother) Arabella, baby found real mother, we did good by returning him, God will give us our own.

MRS. ARABELLA SEDINAM LARYEA: (crying but smiling, holding Frederick's hand) Yes, let's go home, maybe we adopt legally now from Social Welfare, not through doctor.

NARRATOR: FINAL WORDS ON SCREEN - 15,000 babies are stolen every year in Africa. Some mothers never find them. A mother's love never forgets. Some rich women buy babies thinking legal but it is stolen. Check yellow kente cloth always. This is Tales By Zeenat Film. ZeenatFlix GH.

THE FOOD SELLER.short: In Lekki, Monica's food joint is so sweet, customers get addicted like drugs. But okada rider Emeka peeps through her window at 5:30am and sees her pouring a white gallon with hairs inside into her stew pot. What is inside?
THE FOOD SELLER.long:
Everyone in Lekki queues for Monica's Special Food - by 11am, it finishes. But anyone who eats once must come back every day, like their spirit is tied.

Okada rider Emeka notices the addiction. One morning he peeps through her kitchen window and sees a white gallon with blue cover, foam and hairs floating inside, pouring into her black cooking pot.

That night he returns. The smell is like cemetery. Monica confesses: "Baba from Ijebu said dead body bathing water will make customers never leave."

This Lagos horror is based on real juju food joints in Nigeria. If food is too sweet, check the hidden gallon.
THE FOOD SELLER.full:
NARRATOR: Lekki, Lagos, Nigeria. Monica's roadside food joint is the most famous. Sign: MONICA'S SPECIAL FOOD. By 11am, all food finishes.

MONICA: (serving food) Oya come chop! My special jollof! My special stew!

EMEKA: (okada rider, bringing passengers) Monica your food too sweet o! Why everyone who chop here must come back every day like addiction?

TUNDE: (customer) Since I start to chop here, I no fit miss one day!

NARRATOR: SCENE 2 - The Curiosity. 5:30am morning.

EMEKA: (washing okada early) I come early wash my okada. (Sees Monica) Wait, why Monica dey carry large black nylon bag like thief? She dey look left and right.

MONICA: (looking left and right like thief, quickly enters kitchen behind food joint) Make nobody see me.

EMEKA: Something dey inside that bag.

NARRATOR: SCENE 3 - Peeping Through Window.

EMEKA: (parks okada, walks to kitchen window) Let me peep through window and small hole in wall.

MONICA: (inside kitchen, brings out WHITE GALLON with blue cover from black bag, hands shaking)

EMEKA: (eyes popping) White gallon? With blue cover? Why her hands dey shake?

NARRATOR: SCENE 4 - The Pouring. Most important poster moment.

MONICA: (opens gallon, inside strange water with foam and hairs floating) Baba said small small only.

EMEKA: (eyes wide through window, popping through as you marked in poster) What is inside? Foam? Hairs floating? Inside water?

MONICA: (brings large black cooking pot - same pot she uses for stew, pours gallon water inside pot)

EMEKA: Jesus! She pour am inside black pot! Same pot she dey use cook stew for customers!

NARRATOR: SCENE 5 - She Senses Him.

MONICA: (suddenly stops, looks toward window) Who dey there?!

EMEKA: (runs hide behind generator, heart beating fast) Gbim! Gbim! She hear me?

MONICA: (checks outside, sees nobody) Nobody dey. I dey fear too much.

NARRATOR: Monica goes back lock door.

NARRATOR: SCENE 6 - Midnight Investigation.

EMEKA: (12am midnight, cannot sleep, wears dark clothes, returns to food joint) I no fit sleep. That gallon dey worry me. I must go back.

MONICA: (kitchen light on, sleeping inside)

EMEKA: (opens door small) White gallon still on table, open. (Smells) Chai! Terrible smell! Like cemetery! Like dead body bathing water!

NARRATOR: SCENE 7 - The Confrontation.

EMEKA: (pushes door enter) Monica! What is inside this gallon? Tell truth now!

MONICA: (shocked, jumps) Emeka! You! How you enter my kitchen?

EMEKA: What is inside this white gallon with blue cover? Tell truth or I shout!

MONICA: (crying, kneeling) Please don't tell anybody! Please! Baba from Ijebu gave me idea. He said if I use dead body bathing water mix in my food, customers will never stop coming. Their spirit will tie to my food joint!

EMEKA: Dead body bathing water! You dey use dead body water cook for people!

MONICA: I suffered! My food joint no dey sell before! No customers! Baba said go cemetery midnight, collect water used to bathe dead body, mix small small in food, customers will never stop coming!

NARRATOR: SCENE 8 - The Secret Revealed Full.

MONICA: I go cemetery for Ijebu midnight, I beg mortuary man, he give me water used to bathe dead body. I pour small small inside stew. Since then, my food joint full! By 11am food finish!

EMEKA: You wicked! You use juju tie people spirit!

NARRATOR: SCENE 9 - The Victims.

EMEKA: (calls Tunde and two other customers) Tunde come! Come hear wetin Monica dey do!

TUNDE: (shocked) Since I start to chop here, I see dead man for dream calling me come cemetery! I think say na malaria!

WOMAN: My child sick after eating here! Stomach dey pain everyday!

EMEKA: See! Na dead body water!

NARRATOR: SCENE 10 - Exposing Her.

EMEKA: (morning, crowd gather in front of MONICA'S SPECIAL FOOD, carries white gallon) Everybody come! Come see!

CROWD: What is happening?

EMEKA: (pours white gallon on ground in front of everybody) See! Na dead body water she dey use cook for you! No be Maggi! See hairs inside! See foam! No be stew!

CROWD: (shouting) Ah! Jesus! Monica! You wicked!

PEOPLE: (running from tables, some vomiting) I dey vomit! I don chop dead body water!

MONICA: (kneeling beg) Forgive me! Hunger cause am! I no get customers before!

NARRATOR: SCENE 11 - The Downfall.

MAMA NKECHI: (65, old woman) Monica, you young girl but your heart old with evil. Food business na blessing from God, you turn am to curse with dead body water.

MONICA: Mama Nkechi please!

MAMA NKECHI: Pack your things. No okada go stop here again. No man go chop here again.

NARRATOR: Monica packs things, her food joint empty. Sign MONICA'S SPECIAL FOOD falling.

NARRATOR: SCENE 12 - The Lesson.

EMEKA: (one week later, warning people on his okada with megaphone) My brothers and sisters for Lekki! No be every sweet food be good food! Some pot get hidden gallon! If food too sweet and addictive like drug, check am!

NARRATOR: Last shot: White gallon for dustbin, flies around, terrible smell, Monica waka go village with shame, bag on head, no customers.

MORAL: If food too sweet and people addicted like drug, check am - e get wetin dey inside! Some recipes should stay buried!

THE SLAVE TRADE.short: 1703, Cape Coast Castle Dungeon. Ayele with baby Kofi chained at the Door of No Return. In her hand, a small black smoking pot that refused to cross the sea for 100 years - and today it will stop the white man's ship.
THE SLAVE TRADE.long:
1703 Gold Coast, 200 Ghanaians locked in Elmina dungeon. Ayele holds her 6-month-old Kofi, about to be shipped to America as slaves.

Old Nana Esi gives her a black smoking pot: "Any slave who holds it with true heart, the sea will reject the ship."

At the Door of No Return, Ayele refuses to cross. The pot smoke turns to ancestors, the sea boils, the white man's ship shakes and cannot move.

History says many Ghana mothers chose to die in Ghana than be slaves across sea. What did Ayele do when the pot told her "Break me"?
THE SLAVE TRADE.full:
NARRATOR: 1703, Cape Coast, Elmina dungeon, chain on foot as poster, sea light from Door of No Return.

AYELE: Kofi, they will take us across sea. We will never see Ghana again.

NANA ESI: (gives black smoking pot as poster) This pot is ancestors. It refused to cross sea for 100 years. Hold with true heart, sea will reject ship. Hold till smoke finishes.

AYELE: This small pot can stop ship?

NANA ESI: Ancestors inside smoke. Hold like baby.

CAPTAIN WHITE: Bring slaves to ship! Today you cross Door of No Return! You never see Ghana again!

MAMA AFRIKA: No! Our children!

AYELE: (at arch door light as poster, holding Kofi + pot) I will not cross. My baby will not cross. Ghana is our blood. This pot refuses!

CAPTAIN WHITE: Small pot juju? Move! (tries push, smoke thick) What smoke!

WHITE SAILORS: Captain! Sea angry! Ship cannot move!

CAPTAIN WHITE: What inside pot?!

ANCESTORS: (faces in smoke behind Ayele) This mother and child belong to Ghana soil. Sea refuses chains. Pot that refused sea has chosen her.

ALL SLAVES: Kneel! Ancestors!

CAPTAIN WHITE: (tries take pot) Give me pot! Aaaa! It burns! Devil!

AYELE: Not devil. Ancestors. Burns those who steal us.

CAPTAIN WHITE: Choose! Throw pot to sea and cross as slave to America, or stay dungeon die here with pot!

AYELE: My baby will not be slave. I choose Ghana soil.

MAMA AFRIKA: Remember us! Tell Ghana we tried!

AYELE: I will tell! Pot will remember!

NARRATOR: Ship leaves without Ayele and Kofi! Sea calm! Others forced cross crying. Captain locks dungeon.

CAPTAIN WHITE: Die here with pot!

NARRATOR: Night, no food water, chain as poster, pot smoke stops, Kofi cries.

KOFI BABY: Waa!

NANA ESI: Pot...

ANCESTORS: (pot glows red) AYELE! BREAK POT! BREAK US AND WE FREE YOU! BUT OUR 100 YEARS POWER FINISH FOREVER! If you don't break, you and baby die tonight!

AYELE: Forgive ancestors! Baby must live! (lifts pot high, hits stone) KPAA! POT BREAKS! Smoke explodes x100!

ANCESTORS: WE ARE FREE!

NARRATOR: Chain as poster BREAKS BY ITSELF! Wall cracks! Sea water enters!

AYELE: Chain broken!

ANCESTORS WARRIOR: Follow smoke to small hole behind stones! Old escape tunnel 1482! White men don't know! Go!

AYELE: (carries Kofi kente on back as poster, holds shards, crawls through hole where sea light comes) Kofi hold mama! We go home!

NARRATOR: 10 minutes crawling, then LIGHT! Forest!

CAPTAIN WHITE: (morning returns) Where witch mother? (sees empty, broken shards smoking + broken chain + kente) Empty! Chain broken! How?

SOLDIER: Captain, tunnel! Old tunnel here!

CAPTAIN WHITE: Close with stones! If slaves know, all escape!

NARRATOR: Forest near Elmina, Ayele, Nana Esi, 7 mothers build hidden village.

AYELE: Kofi, we free. Ghana soil.

NANA ESI: Shards still smoking! Ancestors still inside!

AYELE: Buries shards under Baobab tree. Tree smokes. Here children never slaves.

NARRATOR: 20 years later 1723, Kofi 20 warrior, kente like mother poster, holding shard.

KOFI: Mama, white men came again.

AYELE: Use shard.

KOFI: (holds shard, smoke) White men fear smoke! Run! Never enter forest. Forest becomes FREE VILLAGE.

CAPTAIN WHITE: (old, sees Kofi) You! That baby from dungeon!

KOFI: I am Kofi, son of Ayele, son of Ghana. Pot that refused sea is my mother pot.

CAPTAIN WHITE: No! That pot again! (runs) Never returns.

TOUR GUIDE: (Cape Coast today 2026, arch as poster) This is Door of No Return. Under Baobab outside, black shards still smoking small. Grandmothers say pieces of pot that refused sea 1703.

TOURIST: True?

TOUR GUIDE: In Ghana, Ayele story true. Many mothers broke pot to save babies. That's why some still in Ghana, not America.

AYELE: (70 years, under Baobab, holding grandchild as she held Kofi poster) Grandchild, 1703 I held your father Kofi and black pot at Door as picture. I said NO.

GRANDCHILD: Pot really refused sea?

AYELE: Sea refused pot. Pot chose Ghana. I broke pot, but Ghana never broke.

NARRATOR: Final shot same as poster - Ayele crying brave holding Kofi + pot + chain + Door light.

NARRATOR: Not just Ayele story. Ghana story. 1700s thousands mothers said NO at Door. Some broke pot. Some broke chains. Some chose death in Ghana than slave across sea. That why Ghana free today. Because one mother with baby and small black smoking pot refused to cross sea. Pot still smokes in Cape Coast. Search: ZEENATFLIX 

FINAL WORDS: In memory of all Ghana mothers who refused Door of No Return 1700s. Your pot still smokes. Your children still in Ghana. TALES BY ZEENAT NETFLIX ORIGINAL. MORAL: Freedom is not given. It is refused. Like pot refused sea.
